subject.title: tools.deny not enforced for claude-cli backend MCP — agents can call denied MCP tools

question: Which Claude CLI MCP enforcement boundary should OpenClaw own for denied or narrowed MCP tools?
rationale: The current gap is a security boundary bug, but the prior direct PR showed that a plausible pre-write filter can widen exact MCP tool permissions unless maintainers choose the permanent representation and fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Pre-handoff effective MCP surface
options.body: Filter or proxy the generated Claude MCP surface from the resolved per-agent OpenClaw policy, preserve deny-wins semantics, and fail closed for narrower restrictions that cannot be represented exactly.

options.title: Claude native deny mapping only
options.body: Map OpenClaw MCP deny entries into Claude `--disallowedTools` where possible, accepting tighter coupling to Claude permission semantics and separate generated-config behavior.

options.title: Declare unsupported combinations
options.body: Keep the strict generated MCP config path but reject or warn on `claude-cli` plus unenforceable MCP restrictions until a stronger bridge lands.

recommendation.title: Pre-handoff effective MCP surface
recommendation.body: Filter or proxy the generated Claude MCP surface from the resolved per-agent OpenClaw policy, preserve deny-wins semantics, and fail closed for narrower restrictions that cannot be represented exactly.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest historical ownership signal for the Claude CLI loopback MCP bridge and shared bundle MCP config paths.
